comment: Frame 020, printed p. 14: the cities of the third clime continued, entries 165-180: Hajar, al-Baḥrayn and the ports of the Gulf, Mahrūbān, Sīnīz, Jannābā, Sīrāf, Nāthin and Tīz on the sea, Kirmān, Dizak in the mountains, al-Daybul on the sea, Armābīl, Kābul, a city on the mountain, Diyār Shatī and Qūlī. Four lines of the editor's footnotes.

variants: L03: at entry (1211) the name مهروبان is written ماهروان.
L04: the manuscript reads سينير, without the dot of the ز.
L05: the manuscript reads حماٮا for جنّابا; at entry (1211) the name is written جنانا.
L06: the manuscript reads سراف, without the ي.
L07: the manuscript reads نابن, with the variant reading ٮالى; at entry (1211) the name is written ناين.
L10: the manuscript reads ذزك, with ذ for the د.
L11: the manuscript reads الدسل, and so does entry (1210).
L13: the degrees of the latitude are unclear in the manuscript and are supplied from S and from Yāqūt (IV, 220).
observations: The table goes on from frame 019 without a heading, again with one longitude and the seven columns of the earlier pages: the cities of the third clime, entries 165-180, all with numbers of Suhrāb, [١٣٠]-[١٤٥]. Only entries 165 and 178 have the word «مدينة».
L05: «جنّابا», with a shadda over the ن. L07: «ناثن»: the three dots of the ث are printed as one mark, narrow above and wide below, as on frame 013 (L14).

L14: the first letter of «ڡرسس», a loop raised above the line and joined to the ر, is printed without dots: the loop of ف or ق (an initial م sits on the line); transcribed so. The editor's notes do not comment on it.

L15: «ديار شتى»: the ش stands 15 px from the end of the tail of the ر, where the spaces between the words of the names on this page measure 21-29 px, and within a word the letter after ر stands over its tail; transcribed with the space.
L16: «قولى»: the stroke of the ل rises 32 px above the line, where the other ل of the names rise 36-47 px and the teeth about 22 px; there is no dot below it; transcribed ل.

Letters printed without their dots in the numerals, transcribed so: ڡ (L07), the isolated loop of ف or ق; ڡٮ (L08), the loop and, close after it, the small tooth and the bowl of a final ب without its dot, narrower than ڡٮ on frame 012 (L13) and wider than the isolated ڡ of L07; ڡح (L14, L15), the loop without dots; صٮ (L11), the final ب without its dot; كٮ (L12, the degrees of the latitude), the ك joined to a final ب without its dot; ٮه (L12, the minutes of the longitude), a tooth joined to a final ه. With their dots: صب (L12); ق (L13) and قد (L16), the ق with its two dots; نه (L01, the minutes of the latitude), the ن with its dot.
L05: the degrees of the longitude, عر: in these numerals the editor reads ر as ز, 7 (introduction, frame 196, p. XVII); transcribed ر as printed.
L13: the editor's note mark i stands after the degrees of the latitude, كح.
The page number «— ١٤ —» stands at the foot, centred.
copy_matter: A fine dark hairline, one or two pixels wide, crosses the ج of «الجبل» in entry 174 (L10) and runs down to the left below the line; a fibre or a scratch, not a stroke of the type.
